title: Cellular monitoring: network events, geofence anomaly detection and audit logs

prose.text: Three views cover what happens to SIMs after deployment: network events, anomaly detection and the audit log.

prose.label: Network events.
prose.text: {{network-events}} {{network-event-fields}} {{event-details-fields}} {{event-json-log}} Tower-location history built from network events is an API read: [[zscaler-cellular.api.wire-notes:tower-history]].

prose.label: Anomaly detection.
prose.text: {{geofence-detection}} {{location-groups}} {{api-policy-type-geofence-only}} Group, dashboard and policy pages are in [[zscaler-cellular.anomaly-policies]]. The console's policy page says geofencing is the only policy type currently available ([[zscaler-cellular.anomaly-policies:policy-config]]); whether a later release adds others is open {{gap:non-geofence-anomalies}}.

prose.label: Retention.
prose.text: The Cellular logs-and-fair-use page gives a retention period and NSS streaming for Cellular logs ([[shared.logs-fair-use.log-retention:cellular]]), but no captured page ties them to the Network Events or Audit Logs pages; per-event JSON download is the only export the console pages state. Whether either console log is kept that long or can reach a SIEM is open {{gap:retention-and-export}}.

event-details-fields.statement: The Network Event Details drawer, opened by clicking an event's ICCID, shows ICCID, SIM Name, IMSI, Country, Operator, Timestamp, IP Address, Source System, Location Details (LAC, CID, MCC, MNC), RAT Type, Data Cap Reached, Event Name, Session ID, SIM ID and SIM EID, plus the Connection Status Log.

quotes: ICCID: The Integrated Circuit Card Identifier assigned to the SIM.
SIM Name: The name or alias assigned to the SIM.
IMSI: The International Mobile Subscriber Identity associated with the SIM.
Country: The country where the event occurred.
Operator: The telecom operator managing the network connection.
Timestamp: The exact date and time when the event occurred.
IP Address: The public or private IP address assigned to the SIM during the session when the event occurred.
Connection Status Log: Provides options to view, download, and copy network event details in JSON format.
Source System: The system or node responsible for the event.
Location Details: Including Location Area Code (LAC), Cell Identifier (CID), Mobile Country Code (MCC), and Mobile Network Code (MNC).
RAT Type: The Radio Access Technology used for the network connection (e.g., LTE, 5G).
Data Cap Reached: Indicates whether the SIM has exceeded the allocated data usage limit.
Event Name: The type of event that occurred, such as session initiated, authorized, or disconnected (e.g., DATA_SESSION_ONLINE).
Session ID: A unique identifier assigned to the session.
SIM ID: A unique identifier assigned to the SIM card used in the device.
SIM EID: A unique identifier for the embedded SIM (eSIM) used in the device.
Locate the event of interest in the table and click ICCID.

event-json-log.statement: The Connection Status Log in the Event Details drawer lets you view, download and copy the network event details in JSON format.

quotes: Connection Status Log: Provides options to view, download, and copy network event details in JSON format.

network-events.statement: The Network Events page logs network and authorization events for all SIMs provisioned to the organization, with time filters, so SIM transitions between online and offline can be tracked.

quotes: It provides detailed insights into network events and authorization events for each SIM.
View a list of records of network events for all SIMs provisioned to your organization.
Track SIM transitions between online and offline states to ensure consistent network availability and performance.
Apply time filters to view log entries specific to that period.

network-event-fields.statement: Each network event shows ICCID, recorded time, EID (only when eSIMs are listed), IMSI, country, operator, a category of session start, session end, online/offline status or authorization, an event status and an event sub status.

quotes: ICCID: The Integrated Circuit Card Identifier is a globally unique identifier assigned to each SIM card.
Recorded at: The date and time when the network event occurred.
IMSI: The International Mobile Subscriber Identity is a unique number assigned to each mobile subscriber.
Country: The geographical location (country) where the event was recorded.
EID: The Embedded Identity Document is a unique identifier for eSIMs. This is shown only if eSIMs are listed.
Operator: The network operator handling the connectivity.
Category: The type of event (session start, session end, online/offline status, or authorization).
Event Status: The status of the network event.
Event Sub Status: The additional status details of the network event.

geofence-detection.statement: Anomaly detection uses metadata, geolocation and network usage patterns to detect when tracked devices move beyond a defined geofence; once a SIM Location Group's geofence is linked to an enabled policy, movement outside the boundary is flagged as a violation.

quotes: The anomaly detection leverages metadata, geolocation insights, and network usage patterns to continuously monitor tracked devices and detect when they move beyond a defined geofence area.

Administrators configure SIM Location Groups to define geofences within each group. After being linked to a policy and enabled, Zscaler Cellular tracks the device's activity in real time and flags any movement outside the permitted boundary as a violation.

location-groups.statement: A SIM Location Group defines a geofence and the SIM-enabled devices to be monitored within it, and these groups form the basis for network anomaly detection policies; the Anomaly Dashboard gives visibility into policy configurations and detects anomalies when devices operate beyond the designated geofence area.

quotes: Administrators set up SIM Location Groups by defining a specific geofence area for each group and assigning the number of SIM-enabled devices to be monitored within that boundary.
These groups form the basis for network anomaly detection policies
The Anomaly Dashboard provides detailed visibility into policy configurations.
It detects anomalies when devices operate beyond the designated geofence area

audit-scope.statement: Cellular audit logs record administrative actions in the Cellular configuration, under Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Cellular.

quotes: Zscaler Cellular audit logs allow you to view a record of all administrative actions performed in the Zscaler Cellular configurations.
On the Zscaler Cellular Audit Logs page (Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Cellular), you can do the following:

audit-fields.statement: Each audit entry shows timestamp, principal ID (the user or system that acted), action (for example Create or Update), resource type (for example Tag, SIM to Tag Mapping or Anomaly Policy), resource name, resource ID and a view of the changes.

quotes: Timestamp: The date and time when the action occurred.
Principal ID: The user or system that performed the action.
Action: The type of operation performed, such as Create or Update.
Resource Type: The type of resource affected (for example, Tag, SIM to Tag Mapping, or Anomaly Policy).
Resource Name: The name of the affected resource.
Resource ID: The unique identifier of the resource.
View Changes: View details of the configuration changes.

api-policy-type-geofence-only.statement: The API contract's operation to create an anomaly policy takes a `policyType` whose only value is `geoFencing`, and the policy list filter has the same single value.

retention-and-export.title: Retention, export and streaming of network events and audit logs
retention-and-export.detail: The Network Events and Audit Logs articles state page-size controls and a per-event JSON download (claim event-json-log) but no retention period or bulk export. The Cellular logs-and-fair-use page states 180 days for logs, six months for audit logs and NSS streaming (shared.logs-fair-use.log-retention:cellular), but it does not say those logs are the ones behind the Network Events or Audit Logs pages.
retention-and-export.blocks: answering how far back Cellular events can be investigated and whether they can reach a SIEM

non-geofence-anomalies.title: Anomaly types other than geofence in later releases
non-geofence-anomalies.detail: The policy configuration article says geofencing is the only policy type currently available (zscaler-cellular.anomaly-policies claim policy-config), and the API accepts only the `geoFencing` policy type (claim api-policy-type-geofence-only). Whether a later release adds other anomaly types such as usage-based ones is not stated.
non-geofence-anomalies.blocks: answering whether usage spikes or other behavior raise Cellular anomalies
